ASSISTED BRIEFING

A clearer view of the week.

Rule-based analysis · No live AI model connected

Select a team and generate a briefing grounded in the displayed metrics.
Explore the data and calculation rules

SLA target ≥ 90%. Risk if backlog grows or SLA falls below target. Resolution rate = resolved ÷ opened. SLA is weighted by resolved requests. Prior-period comparisons use the immediately preceding equally sized window.

The business problem

Operational reporting often requires manual review across teams. Leaders need a traceable view of demand, delivery, and emerging service risks.

The approach

Calculate metrics first, apply transparent risk rules, then produce a briefing with recommendations tied to those findings.

Demonstrated outcome

A repeatable reporting prototype with interactive filters and inspectable evidence. No production savings or business impact are claimed.

  1. No activity yet.

Deterministic keyword classifier, not a live agent. No email is sent, no ticket is created, and no input leaves this page. Do not enter personal or confidential information.

The business problem

Reading, categorizing, and routing repetitive requests consumes attention and creates inconsistent handoffs.

The approach

Validate input, return structured classification and a response draft, and require a human to authorize the exact result.

Demonstrated outcome

A visible approval workflow with a session activity log. Ambiguous requests route to manual triage; every action remains simulated.

UNDER THE SURFACE

Simple architecture. Deliberate boundaries.

01 / Operations

Fictional dataset → Filter & aggregate → Risk rules → Dashboard & briefing

JavaScript calculates the metrics locally. The summary uses those same results, keeping every statement traceable.

02 / Workflow

Validate → Classify → Draft → Human approval → Simulated action

Structured results separate category, priority, destination, and response. Changing input clears the pending approval.

HTML / CSSJavaScriptSVG chartsStructured outputsHuman oversight
How this grows into a live AI solution

Add a small Python FastAPI service between the browser and an AI provider. The server holds the API key in environment variables, validates both inputs and model outputs, limits request size and rate, and returns a fixed response schema. Treat incoming requests as untrusted content. Add authenticated approval records before integrating any real business system.

Current version: no external APIs, no API keys, no server persistence. A production version needs access controls, durable audit logs, privacy review, monitoring, and evaluation of model errors. Prompt wording alone is not a security boundary.
